lines.en: Leo, you look tired. Have you finished the report yet?
lines.pt: Leo, você parece cansado. Você já terminou o relatório?

lines.en: Not yet. I have had three meetings this week, so I haven’t had time.
lines.pt: Ainda não. Tive três reuniões esta semana, então não tive tempo.

lines.en: I have already sent my part. I’ll help you as soon as I finish this email.
lines.pt: Eu já enviei minha parte. Vou ajudar você assim que terminar este e-mail.

lines.en: Thanks. While I write the summary, could you check the numbers?

lines.en: Sure. I have never seen such a busy week in this office.
lines.pt: Claro. Nunca vi uma semana tão cheia neste escritório.

lines.en: I know. Although I am tired, I am going to go running tomorrow.
lines.pt: Eu sei. Embora esteja cansado, vou correr amanhã.

lines.en: Really? I have just heard that it will snow in Denver.
lines.pt: Sério? Acabei de ouvir que vai nevar em Denver.

lines.en: Then I’ll run indoors. I must stay healthy because the deadline is Friday.
lines.pt: Então vou correr em local fechado. Preciso me manter saudável porque o prazo é sexta.

lines.en: Right. Have you called the client about the new date?
lines.pt: Certo. Você ligou para o cliente sobre a nova data?

lines.en: I’ll call him as soon as we finish. He has already agreed to a meeting.
lines.pt: Vou ligar assim que terminarmos. Ele já concordou com uma reunião.

lines.en: Good. After the meeting, let’s have lunch while we plan next week.
lines.pt: Bom. Depois da reunião, vamos almoçar enquanto planejamos a próxima semana.

items.wrong: I call you as soon as I will finish.

facts.big: I have just… / as soon as / while
facts.label: Revisão da semana
facts.sub: Use o present perfect para ações recentes, going to e will para planos e os conectores as soon as, while, because e although para ligar ideias.

facts.label: Acabei de…
facts.sub: Use have/has + particípio com just, already, yet e never: I have just heard the news. Have you finished the report yet? I have never seen such a busy week.

facts.label: Vou fazer
facts.sub: Use going to para planos e will para decisões: I am going to go running tomorrow. I’ll run indoors. Use I’ll como resposta rápida a um problema.

compare.ask: I’ll call him as soon as I finish.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “assim que eu terminar” com o verbo no futuro do subjuntivo.
compare.tip: Diga: “I’ll call him as soon as I finish.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use o presente depois de as soon as, when e while: I’ll call him as soon as I finish. O will fica só na outra parte.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.

extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: I have just finished is a present perfect sentence.
We say “I will call you as soon as I will finish.”
items.why: We say as soon as I finish.

items.s: While means at the same time as.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: I have just finished is a present perfect sentence. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “I will call you as soon as I will finish.” → Falso (We say as soon as I finish.)
While means at the same time as. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 2/2

items.s: We say “Although I am tired, but I will go.”
items.why: We do not use but with although.

items.s: A deadline is a time to finish something.

extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: We say “Although I am tired, but I will go.” → Falso (We do not use but with although.)
A deadline is a time to finish something. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

paragraphs: It is a snowy Wednesday in Denver, and the office is full of noise. Frank sits at his desk with a big cup of coffee. His colleague Leo walks in with a heavy bag. The week has been very long for everyone. There is a lot of work, and the schedule is full. Frank wants to know how Leo is doing.

“Leo, you look tired. Have you finished the report yet?” says Frank. “Not yet. I have had three meetings this week, so I haven’t had time.” says Leo. “I have already sent my part. I’ll help you as soon as I finish this email.” says Frank.
